meta.trial_name: ALLHAT-LLT (Antihypertensive and Lipid-Lowering Treatment to Prevent Heart Attack Trial, Lipid-Lowering Trial)
meta.drug: pravastatin 40 mg/day (open label) vs usual care
meta.sponsor: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)
meta.mechanism: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin) lowering LDL-C; compared with usual care, in which physicians could prescribe lipid-lowering drugs (17% of usual-care participants on statins by year 4)
meta.indication: prevention of all-cause mortality in older (>=55 y) hypertensive adults with moderate hypercholesterolemia (LDL-C 120-189 mg/dL, or 100-129 mg/dL with known CHD) and at least one additional CHD risk factor

n_randomized.quote: were randomized to pravastatin (n = 5170) or to usual care (n = 5185)
n_randomized.note: Abstract read verbatim on PubMed. 'Ambulatory persons (n = 10 355), aged 55 years or older'. Original plan was 20,000 (design paper S4).

median_followup.note: MEAN, not median: 4.8 years x 12 = 57.6 months. Full text: 'The mean (SD) duration of follow-up was 4.8 (1.3) years (maximum, 7.8 years).' CTT 2010 (S6) Table 1 lists median follow-up in survivors of 4.9 years.

primary_endpoint.quote: The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, with follow-up for up to 8 years.
primary_endpoint.note: Secondary outcomes: nonfatal MI or fatal CHD combined (CHD events), cause-specific mortality, cancer. Unchanged from the 1996 design (S4).

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age >=55 with hypertension and >=1 additional CHD risk factor (ALLHAT participants); fasting calculated LDL-C 120-189 mg/dL (100-129 mg/dL if known CHD); triglycerides <350 mg/dL; judged by their physicians not to need lipid-lowering drugs
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) of 120 to 189 mg/dL (100 to 129 mg/dL if known CHD) and triglycerides lower than 350 mg/dL
inclusion_key_criteria.note: NHLBI release (S2): 'they had moderately elevated blood cholesterol but were judged by their doctors not to need cholesterol-lowering medication.' Mean age 66, 49% women, 38% black, 23% Hispanic, 14% history of CHD, 35% type 2 diabetes.

planned_events.unit: deaths (expected in usual care group, revised power calculation)
planned_events.quote: the estimate (625) used in the revised power calculation for a sample size of 10 000
planned_events.note: Read via WebFetch of the jamanetwork.com full-text page (a fetch tool extracted excerpts of at most ~125 characters; punctuation such as italics around P may differ). Observed usual-care deaths 641: 'the number of deaths in the ALLHAT-LLT usual care group (641) differed only slightly from the estimate (625)'. The Methods state no planned total number of deaths.

assumed_rrr.note: Read via WebFetch of the jamanetwork.com full-text page (a fetch tool extracted excerpts of at most ~125 characters; punctuation such as italics around P may differ). Original design: 'Originally, the sample size estimate of 20 000 provided 80% power to detect a 12.5% reduction in mortality rate'. Revised because 'a sample size of approximately 10 000 participants was the largest that could be realistically enrolled'.

power.quote: this revised sample size was estimated to provide 84% power to detect a 20% reduction in mortality
power.note: Read via WebFetch of the jamanetwork.com full-text page (a fetch tool extracted excerpts of at most ~125 characters; punctuation such as italics around P may differ). Original plan 80% power for a 12.5% reduction with n=20,000. Discussion: 'ALLHAT-LLT lacked the power to discriminate between the expected reductions in mortality and CHD events'.

alpha.quote: in the pravastatin vs usual care group with a 2-sided α = .05.
alpha.note: Read via WebFetch of the jamanetwork.com full-text page (a fetch tool extracted excerpts of at most ~125 characters; punctuation such as italics around P may differ).

stopped_early.quote: ALLHAT-LLT was a randomized, nonblinded, large simple trial conducted from February 1994 through March 2002
stopped_early.note: Read via WebFetch of the jamanetwork.com full-text page (a fetch tool extracted excerpts of at most ~125 characters; punctuation such as italics around P may differ). Not stopped early; ran to planned closeout (Oct 1, 2001 to Mar 31, 2002, Figure 1 legend). Registry S3 primary completion 2002-03. Open label: usual-care physicians could prescribe lipid-lowering drugs.

baseline.note: Table 3 (full text): 145.6 mg/dL pravastatin vs 145.5 usual care; ~3.78 mmol/L (CTT S6 Table 1: 3.76 mmol/L). Calculated LDL-C (Friedewald).

baseline.quote: Baseline mean total cholesterol was 224 mg/dL
baseline.note: Biomarker: total cholesterol. Table 3: 223.7 vs 223.7 mg/dL.
Biomarker: SBP. Table 1 value read via WebFetch: 145 (13.8)/84 (9.8) pravastatin vs 145 (14.0)/84 (9.8) usual care; table value, no sentence to quote.
NOT FOUND: non-HDL-C not reported. Derived estimate only: TC 224 - HDL-C 48 = 176 mg/dL.

biomarker_effects.method: calculated LDL-C (Friedewald) in random preselected subsamples (10% pravastatin, 5% usual care)
biomarker_effects.quote: levels were reduced by 28% with pravastatin vs 11% with usual care
biomarker_effects.note: Comparator is usual care, not placebo: 'placebo_adjusted' means pravastatin minus usual care. Abstract conclusion: 'modest differential in total cholesterol (9.6%) and LDL-C (16.7%)'. Full text (WebFetch): 'At 4 years calculated LDL-C levels decreased by 27.7% in the pravastatin group and by 11.0% in usual care'; 'Mean LDL differences (usual care − pravastatin) were 23.8 mg/dL at 2 years', '24.2 mg/dL at 4 years, and 17.2 mg/dL at 6 years'. Table 3 means at year 4: 104.5 vs 128.7 mg/dL. The 16.7% is the paper's differential in percent change from baseline (27.7 - 11.0).

biomarker_effects.method: CTT collaboration; LDL-C difference at 1 year
biomarker_effects.location: CTT 2010, Table 1 (columns: number of patients, treatment comparison, median follow-up in survivors (years), baseline LDL-C (mmol/L), LDL-C difference at 1 year (mmol/L))
biomarker_effects.note: Read from Europe PMC XML of PMC2988224. Year-4 difference from S1 (24.2 mg/dL) converts to 0.63 mmol/L; year 6 (17.2 mg/dL) to 0.44 mmol/L. change_pct copied from the S1 row. CTT check (derived, not from a source): 0.78^0.54 = 0.87 expected RR for major vascular events; 0.90^0.54 = 0.945 for all-cause mortality.

biomarker_effects.quote: At year 4, total cholesterol levels were reduced by 17% with pravastatin vs 8% with usual care
biomarker_effects.note: Full text: 'total cholesterol levels decreased by 17.2% in the pravastatin group and by 7.6% in usual care'; 'The resultant total cholesterol differential was 9.6%.' Mean differences 25.3 (year 2), 21.6 (year 4), 18.9 mg/dL (year 6). Discussion: 'The resulting 9.6% total cholesterol differential was less than half the average for the 8 other long-term statin trials'.

biomarker_effects.quote: High-density lipoprotein cholesterol increased by 3.3% in the pravastatin group and 2.4% in the usual care group
biomarker_effects.note: Read via WebFetch of the jamanetwork.com full-text page (a fetch tool extracted excerpts of at most ~125 characters; punctuation such as italics around P may differ). change_pct DERIVED as the difference in percent change (3.3 - 2.4 = +0.9 points). Table 3 subsample means (year 4): 48.9 vs 45.9 mg/dL.

DERIVED from Table 3 means read via WebFetch (pravastatin 145.4 vs usual care 166.1 mg/dL at year 4; baseline 150.6 vs 152.8); -20.7 = 145.4 - 166.1, -12.5% = -20.7/166.1. The paper states no triglyceride differential in the text. Year 6: 141.0 vs 143.0 mg/dL.

biomarker_effects.quote: Pravastatin lowered plasma cholesterol levels by 20 percent and low-density-lipoprotein cholesterol levels by 26 percent, whereas there was no change with placebo.
biomarker_effects.note: Pre-readout benchmark from a different trial (WOSCOPS, 1995) for the same drug and dose against placebo; shows what pravastatin 40 mg does without usual-care statin use. WOSCOPS: 31% reduction in coronary events.

biomarker_effects.quote: pravastatin at a dose of 20 mg once daily at bedtime significantly lowered serum low-density lipoprotein cholesterol 26% (4.7 to 3.5 mmol/liter [182 to 135 mg/dl])
biomarker_effects.note: Placebo-controlled lipid study (n=1,062, 1993), not a dose-ranging trial; change from baseline within the pravastatin arm (placebo_adjusted=null); -1.2 mmol/L derived (3.5 - 4.7). 20 mg, not the 40 mg used in ALLHAT-LLT.

hr.unit: relative risk (all-cause mortality, pravastatin vs usual care)
hr.quote: All-cause mortality was similar for the 2 groups (relative risk [RR], 0.99; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.89-1.11; P =.88)
hr.note: Reported as RR (Cox-based per paper). 6-year mortality 14.9% vs 15.3%. CHD events (secondary): RR 0.91 (0.79-1.04), P=.16, 380 vs 421 events. Stroke RR 0.91 (0.75-1.09), P=.31, 209 vs 231. Heart failure RR 0.99 (0.83-1.18). CV death RR 0.99 (0.84-1.16), 295 vs 300 (secondary values read via WebFetch).

events_treatment.quote: There were 631 deaths in the pravastatin group and 641 deaths in the usual care group
events_treatment.note: Read via WebFetch of the jamanetwork.com full-text page (a fetch tool extracted excerpts of at most ~125 characters; punctuation such as italics around P may differ). Also in the NHLBI release (S2): 'There were 631 deaths in the pravastatin group and 641 in the usual care group.' Pravastatin N=5170.

events_control.quote: There were 631 deaths in the pravastatin group and 641 deaths in the usual care group
events_control.note: Usual care N=5185; usual care is not placebo (17.1% on a statin at year 4, 26.1% at year 6, Table 2). Total deaths 1272.

safety_signals.quote: The 6-year incident cancer rates were similar in the 2 groups.
safety_signals.note: Read via WebFetch of the jamanetwork.com full-text page (a fetch tool extracted excerpts of at most ~125 characters; punctuation such as italics around P may differ).

safety_signals.quote: Specific adverse effects data were not collected.

safety_signals.quote: pravastatin showed a significantly more favorable effect on CHD events (RR, 0.73 vs 1.02) in blacks than in nonblacks
safety_signals.note: Read via WebFetch of the jamanetwork.com full-text page (a fetch tool extracted excerpts of at most ~125 characters; punctuation such as italics around P may differ). Stroke excerpt: 'Parallel analyses for stroke showed a significantly less favorable effect (RR, 1.12 vs 0.74) in blacks than in nonblacks'. NHLBI release: 'Results for death rates did not differ by age, gender, race, or the presence of type 2 diabetes.'

safety_signals.value: Post hoc (2017): in primary-prevention participants aged >=75, all-cause mortality HR 1.34 (0.98-1.84), P=.07, nonsignificant trend toward harm
safety_signals.quote: 1.34 (95% CI, 0.98-1.84; P = .07) for adults 75 years and older
safety_signals.note: Han et al., JAMA Intern Med 2017, post hoc analysis of 2867 participants >=65 without ASCVD; all >=65: HR 1.18 (0.97-1.42), P=.09. Abstract read verbatim on PubMed. Not a prespecified ALLHAT-LLT analysis.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: HMGCR (statin target) LDL-lowering variants protect against cardiovascular events, with the same effect per unit LDL-C as PCSK9 variants
genetics.effect: OR 0.81 (0.72-0.90) per 10 mg/dL lower LDL-C for the HMGCR score
genetics.quote: Variants in PCSK9 and HMGCR were associated with nearly identical protective effects on the risk of cardiovascular events per decrease of 10 mg per deciliter (0.26 mmol per liter) in the LDL cholesterol level: odds ratio for cardiovascular events, 0.81 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.89) for PCSK9 and 0.81 (95% CI, 0.72 to 0.90) for HMGCR.

genetics.finding: HMGCR variants lower LDL-C and slightly raise type 2 diabetes risk and body weight, mirroring the statin diabetes signal (an on-target effect)
genetics.effect: 0.06 mmol/L lower LDL-C per rs17238484-G allele; T2D OR 1.02 (1.00-1.05) per allele
genetics.quote: The increased risk of type 2 diabetes noted with statins is at least partially explained by HMGCR inhibition.

genetics.finding: LDL-C is causal; CTT meta-analysis of 26 statin trials including ALLHAT-LLT: 22% fewer major vascular events and 10% lower all-cause mortality per 1.0 mmol/L LDL-C reduction
genetics.effect: Major vascular events RR 0.78 (0.76-0.80); all-cause mortality RR 0.90 (0.87-0.93) per 1.0 mmol/L
genetics.quote: Across all 26 trials, all-cause mortality was reduced by 10% per 1·0 mmol/L LDL reduction (RR 0·90, 95% CI 0·87–0·93; p<0·0001)

consensus_explanation.summary: ALLHAT-LLT found no effect of open-label pravastatin 40 mg on all-cause mortality (631 vs 641 deaths; RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.89-1.11) and a nonsignificant 9% reduction in CHD events (RR 0.91, 0.79-1.04) over a mean 4.8 years. The investigators, NHLBI and commentators put this down to the usual-care comparator rather than the biology: usual-care physicians were free to prescribe lipid-lowering drugs, and as positive statin trials and guidelines appeared, statin use in usual care rose to 17% by year 4 and 26% by year 6 (about 30% started lipid-lowering drugs at some point), while 20% of the pravastatin group had stopped the study drug by year 4. The between-arm differential was therefore only 9.6% in total cholesterol and 16.7% in LDL-C (CTT: 0.54 mmol/L at 1 year), less than half that of other statin trials, and the authors judged the results consistent with what that small differential predicts. Recruitment of only half the planned 20,000 participants left the trial underpowered (84% power for a 20% mortality reduction, against an expected benefit around 5% for mortality and 13% for major events at 0.54 mmol/L per CTT), so it could not tell expected and null effects apart. The editorial title 'less is less' and the authors' conclusion that the results are consistent with existing cholesterol guidelines reflect the consensus that ALLHAT-LLT did not refute statin benefit; a 2017 post hoc analysis raised, but did not establish, a concern about starting statins in primary prevention after age 75.

available_before_readout: Design: open-label pravastatin vs usual care, 20,000 planned, all-cause mortality primary, LDL-C 120-189 mg/dL, planned mean 6 years (design paper S4, Am J Hypertens April 1996)
Registry record NCT00000542 first posted 1999-10-28 (S3), describing the cholesterol-lowering trial hypothesis (all-cause mortality, usual-care control)

Pravastatin 20 mg lowers LDL-C 26% in a placebo-controlled study (S9, 1993)

Revised sample size (10,000; 84% power for a 20% reduction) and adherence data (S1)
CTT 2010 LDL-C difference 0.54 mmol/L for ALLHAT-LLT and per-mmol/L benchmarks (S6)

sources.note: Secondary expert summary (page lists 01/01/2002, updated 10/04/2004; pub_date set to the update date). Read via WebFetch. Interpretation: 'The lack of difference in cholesterol reduction likely explains much of the lack of difference in clinical outcomes.' and attributes this to 'the relatively high incidence of statin use in the usual care arm (17% by year 4).'

open_questions: Comparator: usual care, not placebo, and open label. All 'placebo-adjusted' lipid effects are pravastatin minus usual care, diluted by usual-care statin use (8.2% year 2, 17.1% year 4, 26.1% year 6) and pravastatin non-adherence (87% year 2, 80% year 4, 77% year 6 taking study drug).

LDL-C was calculated (Friedewald) only in random subsamples (10% pravastatin, 5% usual care); the 16.7% differential is a difference in percent change at year 4. CTT gives -0.54 mmol/L at 1 year; S1 year-4 mean difference 24.2 mg/dL (0.63 mmol/L), year 6 17.2 mg/dL (0.44 mmol/L).
Full-text numbers (power, planned deaths, adherence, Table 2-4) were read through a fetch tool that returns short excerpts; quotes are verbatim fragments, and table values have no sentence to quote.
Pasternak editorial (S5) read only to its opening paragraph; its argument is represented only by its title.

The primary result is reported as relative risk; it is entered as observed_hr for the calculator. Expected effect (derived from CTT, not from a source): all-cause mortality 0.90^0.54 = 0.945, major vascular events 0.78^0.54 = 0.87; observed mortality RR 0.99 (0.89-1.11) and CHD RR 0.91 (0.79-1.04) include these.
NHLBI announcement original URL now redirects (HTTP 301) to the current NHLBI press-release listing; only the Wayback snapshot (earliest capture 2002-12-18) has the 2002 text.
Readout date: NHLBI release embargoed to 9:30 a.m. ET Tuesday 2002-12-17; JAMA lists the article as published online 2002-12-18 (issue date). The earlier date is used.
Registry NCT00000542 covers ALLHAT as a whole and has no posted results.
